plain: This story is about the rock under the Giza Plateau in Egypt, where the great pyramids stand. A pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm tells it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels, in an episode about an energy grid he says lies beneath the pyramids. He says he has chemical tests of iron veins in the bedrock. He describes them as mineral deposits laid down by hot water deep underground. According to Drumm, these veins are full of rare earth elements, a group of uncommon metals, along with gold and silver. Later in that conversation he adds electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver, and other precious metals, 'everything that you could think of'. The story's title also mentions platinum. On a later episode he speaks more generally of valuable metal deposits. If true, it would suggest the pyramids were built where they are because of what lies in the ground.
